note: Owner anchors 2026-11-11: a regular looking roughly the right way spots a man standing still in the open at 300 m in about 5-15 s (base rate 0.07 per s: median 10 s); a man lying still in crops at 100 m is very hard to spot until he moves or fires. Chance per scan = 1 - exp(-rate x scan time); rate = base x (reference range / range)^2 x exposed size by posture x movement or firing x visibility along the line of sight x where he is looking x optic x skill x stress x light. Moving through vegetation shows at least 15 % of a man (plants move); firing at least 50 % (flash, dust). A man already seen is kept with 200 times the rate (once seen, easy to keep) and forgotten after 6 s unseen. All game values for review in the spotting lab. A man keeps track of at most 6 enemies at a time (the nearest); others he has seen pass into what his side knows (contacts, M3.3). Sensors (review fix): every man has his eyes; a weapon sight adds its kind, an item with a `sensor` (night-vision goggle) adds that; the best applies: factor beyond `fromM`, and light counts as at least `nightLight` (night vision, thermal). Moving or firing inside vegetation: the plants or the flash above him show if the line to the top of the vegetation over him is clear (not through a wood). Contacts (M3.3): seen positions are exact to 1 m + 1 % of range; a shot heard within 1,500 m gives the direction (8 degrees error) and a distance guess (35 % error) — owner: direction at once, position only if seen; a contact is forgotten after 2 minutes, its uncertainty grows 1 m per second of age; a man passes on what he sees or hears to his unit every 10 s at most — by voice within the comms model's voice range after 1 s, by radio after the comms model's delay; a reported position is 5 m less certain; a unit calls out new contacts on the radio at most every 8 s. Smoke (M6.5c): the view through smoke falls by exp(-0.15 per metre): 15 m of smoke leaves about a tenth, a 50 m screen nothing (game value). M7.3 (game values, low): vehicle sights (vehicle-day x8-class optics 2.5 beyond 150 m; vehicle-thermal 2.5 day and night, keeps half its view through ordinary smoke (owner Q7), sees at least 1800 m in fog, x0.85 in rain; vehicle-night-ir image intensifier/IR; vision-block periscopes 0.7) reach 3000 m. Vehicles as targets (seen out to 3000 m): the area their hull and turret boxes show at the observer's aspect / 0.7 m2 (a standing man), x4 moving above 0.5 m/s, x15 firing; a man tracks up to 2 vehicles besides men; a vehicle contact drifts 6 m/s and is forgotten after 300 s; engines heard every 2 s within the noise range x (0.6 + surface noise) x (1 - 0.4 rain), x1.2 downwind, x0.8 upwind. Smoke v2 (M8.1, game values, low): a cloud is a volume: its radius and height grow from 30 % to full over smokeBuildSeconds, it thins to nothing over its last smokeFadeSeconds 20 s, it drifts with the wind (smokeDriftFactor 1: with the air) while its round keeps feeding it at its place (a plume, at most smokeStretchMaxM 200 m long), and only a line of sight below its top passes through it (mortar smoke 15 m, vehicle grenades 8 m, a burning vehicle 30 m). Night and light (M9.1, game values, low): the sun table is for the equinox at about 50 degrees north in local solar time (sunrise about 6:00, sunset about 18:00, light rising through civil twilight to full daylight by 7:00 and falling from 17:00, dark from 19:15 to 4:45); a full moon gives 0.12 (eyes see about as at deep dusk), a new moon nothing (light floor 0.05). At night a man's muzzle flash shows him as if lit to 0.8 for every observer (a night sight or thermal no better), a firing vehicle's gun flash lights it to 0.8 likewise, and a man firing tracers shows up to 3 times more in full darkness. Sensor physics (M9.2, game values, low): a sensor marked thermal sees heat — a man as by eye (x1), a vehicle moving or moved within 10 minutes x1.6 (tracks, engine, exhaust), halted longer x0.8 (cooled, engine idling), firing x2.5, burning x6 — and vegetation lets heat through as visibility^0.5 (a man in crops or a hedge shows more; the better of the best sensor and the best thermal one through the vegetation counts); a man's thermal sight covers 12 degrees either side of where he looks, his goggles 20 (a 40-degree field of view); a still man under a thermal blanket shows its share of his heat. Batteries are reserved (M11.6). M9.4a: drone cameras (drone-day: zoom camera, drone-thermal: radiometric-class thermal; factors and ranges game values, low) look down on men, who show about as much from above in any posture (drone.postureSize, low); a drone's report carries feedErrorM more than a man's sighting (reading the position off the picture); searchFactor: the camera searches its whole footprint, not one man (a rate factor); a man under a tree canopy (vegetation over him higher than canopyAboveM) shows canopyDay of himself to the day camera and canopyThermal to the thermal one (game values, low). M9.4b: a drone in the air as a target: its area (item areaM2) against the sky shows targetContrast times as much as the same area on the ground; seen to seenMaxM; within its noise range men look for it heardLookFactor times as hard; a man engages one he sees within engageM when he has no enemy on the ground; each round fired at it hits with its area over the spread at its range (aim, dispersion and leadErrorShare of its movement during the bullet's flight), at most maxHitChance; aerialAimMrad is the extra aim error of a man firing up at a small aircraft (tracking it, judging its range); killShare of the rounds that hit it bring it down (a round through a rotor blade or an arm may not) (game values, low). Flares (M9.6, game values, low): a burning illumination flare lights the ground below as a point source, illuminance = candela / (height^2 + distance^2) lux; it gives light = illuminance / flareFullLux 20 lux (20 lux counts as full daylight for spotting), at most flareMaxLight 0.6 (a flare-lit field is never as clear as day: harsh shadows, glare); the brightest flare counts, as one more term beside the ambient light, a sensor's own light and a muzzle flash. Sight realism step 3 (2026-11-15, owner: hidden men were seen too easily; game values against the spotting lab; medium for vegetation and stillness, low for firing, rooms and conspicuity; search extracts only): (conceal) a man seen is kept at keepFloorFactor 20 + (keepRateFactor - 20) x exp(-quiet s / keepDecaySeconds 5), quiet = time since he last moved, fired or launched (once he lies still the observer must find him again); each man lying or standing still among plants or in a room has a conspicuity drawn once where he settles (lognormal, mean 1, sigma 0.8: some men blend in well, some do not; the same for every observer), drawn again after he takes another posture or has moved 5 m; a still man in vegetation blends into its backdrop (vegetation.backdrop) and, if it is lower than the point an observer looks at, shows only the part of him above it; thermal sights see heat, not blending, and vegetation thins heat by its heatConcealPerM; a prone man moving slower than 0.6 m/s (crawling) shows 1.6 times as much, not 4; a man lying still shows 1 / (1 + (range / 250 m)^4) of himself to an observer on the ground (grass, furrows and small folds of the ground at a grazing angle: 0.97 at 100 m, 0.72 at 200 m, 0.13 at 400 m; drones and thermal sights are not affected: heat shows through); by day firing shows 1 + 14 / (1 + range / 200 m) times as much (the flash and dust are hard to see far off; the full 15 at night), and through vegetation at least 0.25 of him by day (0.5 in full dark); a man who heard shots (or was told of an enemy) from within 10 degrees of a man's bearing, with the guessed spot within 50 m of him, looks three times as hard there while he is looking for him (the three nearest such directions only: he turns his attention to a few directions, not to every shot on the field); a man inside a house shows 0.25 of himself by day (a dark room; nearer 1 as the light fails), half that again more than 1 m back from the nearest window or door on his floor, and firing from inside shows 6 times as much, not 15. Weapon optics (magnified, telescopic) help only within 10 degrees of where he looks. Sources (search extracts only, no page could be opened here): Van der Burg, Hogervorst, Toet, 'Visual search and target detection in cluttered scenes' (SPIE, search extract): static targets are hard to find against clutter; motion breaks camouflage; FM 21-75 Combat Skills of the Soldier (1984, search extract): shine, shadow, outline, movement; a man in vegetation; crack-thump: the sound of a shot gives the direction to look; Urban operations doctrine (search extracts, e.g. FM 3-06.11): fire from back in a room, not from the window sill; the dark room hides the firer.
